text:
If you’re heading out for sunset, bring the rain jacket. It’s already light rain and misty in Burlington, and the sky should stay gray around 6:38, with a few more showers possible this evening. Rain becomes less likely after midnight, though clouds linger and temperatures settle near 50. On the lake, north winds of 10 to 15 knots will keep waves at 1 to 2 feet, so this isn’t an especially inviting waterfront night.

Tuesday looks like a slow improvement rather than a bright turnaround, with clouds holding much of the day and a high near 63. The forecasters’ discussion leans dry as the departing system pulls away, though the models aren’t perfectly aligned, one keeps a 40 percent shower chance in play. I’d bet on a mostly dry day, but keep a light jacket handy, especially with a north wind of 6 to 9 mph. Plan around a damp evening tonight, then take your outdoor time Tuesday afternoon if the clouds finally start to break.

WCAX METEOROLOGIST (regional station — Burlington relevance only, never their branding): Southerly winds strengthen Thursday ahead of an approaching cold front, pushing unseasonably warm air into Vermont and the North Country. High temperatures in lower elevations will reach the mid-to-upper 70s, with a few spots approaching 80°—putting daily record highs in jeopardy (such as Montpelier’s record of 78° set in 2002). Southerly wind gusts will reach 25 to 30 mph in wide valleys, with gusts approaching 40 mph in the St. Lawrence Valley and sustained 20+ knot winds on Lake Champlain. A cold front brings scattered light showers late Thursday night into Friday (30% chance) with highs near 69°. High pressure brings a bright, crisp Saturday with mostly sunny skies and highs near 63°, before a transient low-pressure system brings returning shower chances Sunday (40% chance, High 64°). Cooler, partly sunny conditions take over next Monday with highs in the upper 50s.
